title: Derived sections through finite pushforward for module sheaves
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $p:Z\to Y$ a finite morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and $M$ a bounded-below complex of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site of $Z$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Direct image $p_*$ on these module sheaves is exact and sends injective objects to injective objects. There is a canonical natural isomorphism $\lambda_{p,M}:R\Gamma(Y,p_*M)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(Z,M)$ [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded]. Its normalization is: for a bounded-below injective resolution $M\to L$, $p_*L$ is a bounded-below injective resolution of $p_*M$, and $\lambda_{p,M}$ is induced by $\Gamma(Y,p_*L)=\Gamma(Z,L)$.

For an arbitrary scheme morphism $h:Y'\to Y$, form $Z'=Y'\times_Y Z$ with projections $g:Z'\to Z$ and $p':Z'\to Y'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $\beta_M:h^{-1}p_*M\to p'_*g^{-1}M$ be the adjoint of the counit map $(p')^{-1}h^{-1}p_*M=g^{-1}p^{-1}p_*M\to g^{-1}M$; inverse image and these adjunctions are the exact module functors of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. The square with horizontal arrows $\lambda_{p,M}$ and $\lambda_{p',g^{-1}M}$ and vertical arrows
$$R\Gamma(Y,p_*M)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{res}_h}R\Gamma(Y',h^{-1}p_*M)\xrightarrow{R\Gamma(\beta_M)}R\Gamma(Y',p'_*g^{-1}M),\qquad R\Gamma(Z,M)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{res}_g}R\Gamma(Z',g^{-1}M)$$
commutes in $D(\operatorname{Mod}\Lambda)$. Here restriction is the map induced by the inverse-image/direct-image unit. Only the displayed canonical mate is used; no base-change isomorphism is a hypothesis of this compatibility assertion.

source.place: Tag 03QP, proposition-finite-higher-direct-image-zero, and derived.tex Tag 015M (lemma-compose-derived-functors): module-valued bounded-complex specialization with explicit unit/counit normalization. No abelian-sheaf-only derived Leray statement is used.

proof.text: The underlying abelian direct image along a finite morphism is exact by [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact]. The module direct image has exactly this underlying functor by [lem-weil-pbc-module-direct-image-left-exact]. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], forgetting module scalars is faithful and preserves kernels and cokernels: it therefore reflects exactness, since the homology of a sequence has zero underlying abelian sheaf exactly when it is zero. Consequently finite direct image is exact on module sheaves. This is an underived argument only.

source.place: Tag 03QP, proposition-finite-higher-direct-image-zero; module direct image is sites-cohomology.tex Tag 071J (section-derived-functors), and coefficient forgetting is sites-modules.tex Tags 03DA (lemma-abelian) and 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits).

proof.text: For every scheme morphism $u$, [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] show that $u_*$ preserves injective module sheaves. Use [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives, lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] to choose a bounded-below injective representative $L$ of $M$. The comparison $M\to L$ may be represented by a quasi-isomorphism of module complexes by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. By Step 1, $p_*L$ represents $p_*M$ and is termwise injective. Both $R\Gamma$ functors are computed on these module complexes by [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded, lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. The equality $\Gamma(Y,p_*L)=\Gamma(Z,L)$ is an equality of complexes of $\Lambda$-modules, with the same differential. It gives $\lambda_{p,M}$. To compare choices, a map into another injective representative is a unique homotopy class by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]; applying $p_*$ and then sections gives the same map as taking sections on $Z$. Hence these identifications commute with comparison maps and with morphisms of $M$, proving canonicity, naturality and the claimed normalization.

source.place: Tags 05TI (lemma-enough-injectives-right-derived), 070I (lemma-K-injective), and 015M (lemma-compose-derived-functors), applied in module categories

proof.text: Finite morphisms are stable under arbitrary base change by [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange], so Steps 1 and 2 apply to $p'$. Exactness of $g^{-1}$ preserves the lower bound. By [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative, lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] choose a bounded-below injective module complex $J$ on $Z'$ and a module-linear quasi-isomorphism $t:g^{-1}L\to J$. Then $p'_*J$ is termwise injective and $p'_*t$ is a quasi-isomorphism, so it computes $R\Gamma(Y',p'_*g^{-1}L)$. The bottom-right comparison $\lambda_{p',g^{-1}L}$ is the identity $\Gamma(Y',p'_*J)=\Gamma(Z',J)$ from Step 2. In particular all four corners have module-complex models; no assertion that an underlying abelian complex is K-injective has entered.

source.place: Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective); finite base change is morphisms.tex Tag 01WL (lemma-base-change-finite)

proof.text: Use the inverse-image composition comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition] to identify $(p')^{-1}h^{-1}$ with $g^{-1}p^{-1}$. This comparison also applies to constant-$\Lambda$ modules: its naturality commutes with each scalar endomorphism, and [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] supplies the transported actions and the identical underlying units and counits. A section of a constant ring sheaf is locally a constant scalar [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], so commuting with constant scalars proves module linearity locally and hence globally. The comparison's unit equation remains the same equation after forgetting scalars, and faithfulness in [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] proves it in module sheaves. Define $\beta_F$ by the module adjunction from $g^{-1}\varepsilon_{p,F}$ with this comparison. Thus $\beta$ is a natural transformation of module functors, and is the canonical mate in the statement.

source.place: section-pullback: adjunction-mate construction; module linearity follows from naturality and the constant-ring actions

proof.text:
Write $e_u$ for the underived unit section map. We verify $\Gamma(Y',\beta_F)e_h(p_*F)=e_g(F)$ under the section identifications, for a module sheaf $F$ on $Z$. A section $s\in\Gamma(Y,p_*F)$ is, by adjunction, the same section $\widetilde s\in\Gamma(Z,F)$. Equivalently, viewing sections as linear maps from the regular constant module, its transpose is $\widetilde s=\varepsilon_{p,F}\circ p^{-1}s$, with the constant-module identifications. Pulling $s$ along $h$ and applying $\beta_F$ has transpose under $(p')^{-1}\dashv p'_*$ equal to
$$g^{-1}(\varepsilon_{p,F})\circ g^{-1}p^{-1}(s)=g^{-1}(\varepsilon_{p,F}\circ p^{-1}s)=g^{-1}\widetilde s.$$
The first equality is the defining counit formula for $\beta$ from Step 4 and the unit equation for the composition comparison; the last expression is precisely $e_g(F)(\widetilde s)$. This proves the equality on every section as $\Lambda$-linear maps, before deriving. Applied to each $F=L^n$ it proves an equality of chain maps, since all constituent sheaf maps are natural and commute with the differentials.

source.place: section-pullback: unit/counit mate formula, expanded on a global section

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-module-derived-restriction-resolution] first to $u=h$, $I=p_*L$, target $p'_*J$, and $a=p'_*t\circ\beta_L$. It says that the left vertical composite, after the resolution identifications, is the class in $D(\operatorname{Mod}\Lambda)$ of
$$\Gamma(Y,p_*L)\xrightarrow{e_h}\Gamma(Y',h^{-1}p_*L)\xrightarrow{\Gamma(\beta_L)}\Gamma(Y',p'_*g^{-1}L)\xrightarrow{\Gamma(p'_*t)}\Gamma(Y',p'_*J).$$
Apply the same node to $u=g$, $I=L$, target $J$, and $a=t$. The right vertical composite is the class of $\Gamma(Z',t)\circ e_g(L)$. The horizontal maps are identities on the section-complex models by Steps 2 and 3. Step 5 identifies the first three terms of the upper expression with $e_g(L)$, and $\Gamma(Y',p'_*t)=\Gamma(Z',t)$. Thus the two composites are equal as module-linear chain maps and consequently in the module derived category. Naturality of $\beta$ and exactness of all four underived functors identify its component at $M$ with its component at $L$ under $M\to L$, so this proves exactly the displayed square for $M$. No isomorphism assertion for $\beta$ is needed.
